transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Redwood: Maya Patel (AE), Chris Liao (SE)
Customer: Ravi Menon (CTO), Leah Torres (Head of ML), Samir Aziz (Infra Engineer)

Summary (auto): Intake focused on dedicated/reserved GPUs, hotpool prewarm strategy and eviction tolerances. Agreed next steps to run a bench with replayed traffic and share compliance docs.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood here, and with me is Chris our solution engineer. How are you all?
[00:00:07] Ravi (Accelerant): Hey Maya, doing well — thanks, good to be here. We got Leah and Samir on as well.
[00:00:12] Leah: hi, thanks for the invite.
[00:00:15] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: we're hoping to understand your workload shape, isolation and compliance constraints, and then talk through Dedicated capacity patterns — reserved GPUs, hotpool / warm pool behavior and burst strategies. Sound ok?
[00:00:28] Ravi: Yep that works. High level — we run a mix of real-time chat summarization and document ingestion pipelines. Latency sensitive for chat (<= 150 ms token response ideally), but cost matters too. We want to know when Dedicated makes sense vs Hosted.
[00:00:42] Chris (Redwood): Useful. Can you share current qps and token/prediction sizes? Even ballpark helps.
[00:00:49] Samir: Sure, at baseline it's about 12 rps average across small models, but we see spikes up to 220 rps for short bursts, especially after product announcements. Token lengths vary — chat prompts ~60-90 tokens, docs ingestion uses long context batches ~2k tokens for embeddings/analysis.
[00:01:06] Maya: Nice — so the burst factor is roughly 18x. That maps cleanly to needing some reserved capacity plus a hotpool for short high spikes. 
[00:01:15] Leah: Important note — we operate under a data residency constraint for EU customers and we have a KMS requirement for customer keys. So Private or VPC options are on the table.
[00:01:25] Chris: Understood. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; we also have Private deployments for fully air-gapped setups. For the Dedicated offering we can integrate with your KMS and rotate keys via our audit logs.
[00:01:37] Ravi: What about tenancy and eviction? We can't afford noisy neighbor slowdowns on latency critical endpoints.
[00:01:43] Chris: Right — we recommend reserved pools with tenant fencing. In practice that means you get a pool of GPUs logically fenced to your account; hotpool is a smaller warm set that prewarmed models can run on for bursts. Eviction tolerance depends on the fallback: we can route to a slightly smaller model variant or fallback to Hosted with identical model but different instance type.
[00:02:02] Samir: How fast does prewarm happen? If we get a 200 rps burst for 3-5 minutes — do you prewarm new workers fast enough?
[00:02:09] Chris: Prewarm times vary by model size and quantization: for a 7B model quantized to int8 with our continuous batching tuned, warm pool spin-up is ~20-40s to acceptable steady state. For 70B it can be several minutes unless you keep larger hotpool. We also do KV cache prefix reuse which helps subsequent requests.
[00:02:27] Leah: So for our workload (lots of short chat turns) we probably want larger hotpool to avoid the 40s hit. What's the cost tradeoff?
[00:02:35] Maya: That's where Redwood Optimize configs come in — we can run a cost/latency tradeoff analysis. For example, prewarming a hotpool node to reduce tail latency might increase monthly reserved cost by X% but reduce 95th percentile latency by Y ms. We'll send model-specific numbers.
[00:02:52] Ravi: Another question — we do multi-tenant internally, but need strict separation for EU customers. Can we have per-tenant GPU reservations?
[00:02:59] Chris: Yes, you can carve dedicated allocations per tenant group. We support tenant-level quotas and hard fences. There's an operational overhead to many small reservations versus a pooled approach; we usually recommend a hybrid: per-tenant quotas on a main reserved pool plus a small dedicated hotpool for the highest priority tenants.
[00:03:17] Samir: If a reserved node preempts because of maintenance or shortage, what's the fallback? Circuit-breaker?
[00:03:22] Chris: We have a multi-tier fallback: 1) automatic local reschedule within your reserved pool, 2) fallback to a secondary reserved model variant in another AZ/region if configured, 3) optional spillover to Redwood Hosted with encrypted transit — typically used as last resort. All fallbacks can be configured and have SLO indicators.
[00:03:39] Leah: Regarding compliance, do you provide audit logs per token or per request? Our auditors want per-request traceability and proof of key usage.
[00:03:46] Maya: We provide detailed audit logs (per-request metadata) with export hooks to your SIEM. For KMS operations we log key usage with cryptographic metadata. SOC 2 docs will be included in the packet I send.
[00:03:56] Ravi: How about model versions and rollouts — we need canarying for new model builds.
[00:04:01] Chris: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts across reserved pools, A/B split, and automatic rollback on quality regressions. You can pin model versions to pools. For POC we'll suggest a simple 5% canary ramp.
[00:04:12] Samir: Ok, logistics for a POC — we prefer a replay-based bench. We'll provide 2 weeks of traffic and expect you to run it on a representative reserved config.
[00:04:21] Chris: That works. We'll design a benchmark with your RPS, concurrency, and sequence length distribution. We'll also include a warm-pool sizing sweep: try hotpool sizes 1, 2, 4 nodes and measure 95th latency and cost.
[00:04:34] Leah: What about data retention — if we run some logs for the bench, can data be scrubbed automatically?
[00:04:39] Maya: Yes, for POC we can enable ephemeral retention and automatic redaction; production retention policies are customizable per account.
[00:04:46] Ravi: Competitors question — we've talked to bedrock and some infra vendors, one thing flagged was the unknown of preemption during spikes. How does Redwood minimize preemption risk?
[00:04:56] Chris: By reserving capacity and offering preemption policies. Reserved nodes are low preemption; ephemeral capacity is higher. Also our autoscaler prefers local reserved spin-up first before hitting global pools.
[00:05:05] Samir: Any specific kernel/quantization support we should be aware of for our custom models? We have a custom size with LoRA adapters.
[00:05:12] Chris: We support common quant formats (int8, int4) and LoRA adapters — we may need to run a quick compatibility check for your exact custom artifacts but generally supported. We'll include a model-onboarding checklist.
[00:05:24] Maya: I'll add model onboarding and compatibility check to the action items.
[00:05:28] Leah: For hotpool eviction, do you have eviction notifications? We need to log when preemption occurs and if requests were spilled to fallback.
[00:05:35] Chris: Yes, eviction events are surfaced in Console with trace IDs so you can correlate with requests. We can also emit alerts to PagerDuty.
[00:05:42] Ravi: Cost estimates — can you ballpark monthly for baseline reserved capacity to cover 12 rps baseline and sustained 50 rps with 200 rps spikes?
[00:05:52] Maya: We'll need peak-second RPS and model profiles to be precise, but rough guess: a baseline reserved pool sized for 12 rps steady plus a hotpool to absorb the 200 rps spikes will trade between 20-40% higher reserved spend vs minimal reservation. We'll include a couple of scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[00:06:08] Samir: Sounds good. Want to confirm next steps and timeline.
[00:06:12] Maya: Proposed next steps: Maya sends pricing and SOC2/KMS docs by tomorrow; Chris drafts benchmark plan by 05-01; customer uploads traffic sample by 04-30; run bench week of 05-04. Does that work?
[00:06:24] Leah: Yes.
[00:06:25] Ravi: Yes, thanks.
[00:06:27] Maya: Quick recap: we'll size hotpool options, show cost/latency tradeoffs, provide prewarm numbers for 7B and 70B variants, and include tenant fencing patterns. Any other items?
[00:06:40] Samir: Can you also include recommendations for KV cache TTLs for chat workloads?
[00:06:44] Chris: Yep — we'll include KV cache guidance and suggestions to optimize for short-turn latency.
[00:06:49] Leah: Great. Thanks all.
[00:06:51] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the doc pack and scheduling invite for the bench.
[00:06:56] Ravi: Bye.
